items: A message you send while disconnected now shows in the session as not sent yet, and goes out automatically when you reconnect. You can discard it before then.
Clicking a link to a file in an agent reply now opens the file preview instead of reloading the app.
Images in agent replies no longer load on their own. Each shows as a placeholder you can click to open, so a reply cannot send your data anywhere just by including an image.

Guests you invite are now end-to-end encrypted too. An invite link carries your machine’s key, and your machine admits the guest itself, so creating an invite needs that machine online and sharing needs the latest desktop app.

Workflows, steps and recipes that arrive from another machine or another person now need a review before they first run. Settings shows each machine’s sync key so you can trust your own machines once.
Running someone else’s recipe now shows every prompt first, asks you to confirm, runs only in Plan or Ask mode, and pauses between the recipes of a bundle.
“Always allow” now shows exactly what it will allow, and is not offered for commands no allowlist entry could cover safely.
You can set an MCP server’s environment values in Settings → Connections. They stay on that machine and are never synced.
On your phone, a small banner now tells you when the desktop app has an update ready, with a button to restart it.
When the desktop app has an update ready, you can restart into it from the update banner or Settings → Updates.
Typing in a file no longer drops your cursor after the first keystroke, and Save and Discard now sit in the file's header.
The desktop download card no longer shows the macOS "damaged" workaround, since the app is now signed and notarized.
You can now edit a file you open from the file tree, search results or Cmd+P, and save it with Cmd+S.
You can now dictate with your voice into the "Other…" answer of a question and into plan comments.
Lines now shows what changed after an update, and Settings → What's new lists every past update.
The bridge now listens on this computer only and refuses other web pages, so a website you visit or someone on your Wi-Fi cannot reach it.
Agent edits to Claude Code settings and hooks, git hooks and config, MCP configs and shell startup files now always ask first, including through symlinks and shell commands.
Codex sessions can still read your Lines workflows, steps and connections but can no longer change them; make those changes in Lines.
MCP environment values stay on this machine. Earlier versions synced them to Lines storage, so rotate any API key you set there before this update.
Your Lines data folder, transcripts and logs are now readable by your user account only.
Lines now updates itself: new versions download in the background, and a restart installs them.
Saving edits to files from the file viewer now works on your own machine.
The Mac app is now signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS no longer warns when you open a new download.

desktopPending: You can now open, preview and edit any file on your computer from a file link, such as one the agent saved to /tmp or Documents. People you share a session with still only see that session's files.
